advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Broaden FIXED_TMP_REDIRECT (or add a companion pattern) to also catch fixed `/tmp/<name>` assignments, not only `>` redirects, so the guard matches the AGENTS.md guidance it enforces.
evidence: The prior anti-pattern being fixed in this same commit was an assignment `out = "/tmp/diag_matrix.csv"`, which this regex would NOT catch
Litmus: the guard emits an empty `matches` list both when the tree is clean AND when a fixed /tmp path is introduced via assignment rather than `>` redirect
advisory.finding: The guardrail test's FIXED_TMP_REDIRECT regex only matches redirection forms (`>/tmp/name`), not plain fixed-path assignments (e.g. `out = "/tmp/diag_matrix.csv"` or `path=/tmp/x`). A future regression that hardcodes a fixed /tmp path via assignment rather than redirect produces zero matches and the guard reports clean — indistinguishable from genuinely-clean. The guard cannot detect the very class of change (the diag script's own former `out = "/tmp/diag_matrix.csv"`) it is meant to prevent.
scenarios: A later change writes `log_path = "/tmp/foo.log"` (assignment, not redirect) — guard passes silently

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Scope the repo-wide fixed-tmp scan (e.g. exclude fenced code blocks marked as anti-patterns, or narrow to executable files) so documenting the anti-pattern does not fail CI.
evidence: tests/unit/test_per_session_scratch_guidance.py:66-86 walks ROOT/docs, ROOT/src, ROOT/tests, ROOT/.github recursively and asserts `matches == []`
AGENTS.md:324 writes `/tmp/<name>` (angle-bracket, not a real path) specifically so the regex will not match — evidence the guard collides with legitimate documentation of the anti-pattern
advisory.finding: test_repo_guidance_has_no_fixed_tmp_redirects_outside_infra imposes a repo-wide invariant across docs/, src/, tests/, scripts/, and .github/ for all .md/.py/.sh/.yml/.yaml files. Any legitimate future documentation that illustrates the anti-pattern (showing a `>/tmp/name` redirect as an example of what NOT to do) will fail this test. The authors had to deliberately obfuscate AGENTS.md as `/tmp/<name>` (with `<`) to evade the regex, showing the guard already fights legitimate content.
scenarios: A runbook or docs page adds an example command showing the forbidden fixed-tmp redirect for illustration — CI fails on documentation of the rule itself

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Anchor the diag script's default scratch path to the worktree root (or document that it is CWD-relative) to match the AGENTS.md guidance.
advisory.finding: The diag script default output `.rebar/scratch/diag_matrix-{pid}.csv` is CWD-relative, while the AGENTS.md guidance this commit adds prescribes `${PWD}/.rebar/scratch/...` (worktree-anchored). If the script is run from a different working directory the scratch file lands in an unexpected place, diverging from the guidance the same commit establishes.
scenarios: Script invoked from a subdirectory or a different CWD than the repo root — output file is created relative to that CWD, not the worktree root

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Replace the source-grep in test_diag_runaway_matrix_default_output_is_unique_per_process with a behavioral test that runs the default-path derivation for two PIDs (or invokes the module) and asserts distinct paths, plus that DIAG_MATRIX_PATH overrides the default.
evidence: The diag change at docs/experiments/diag_runaway_matrix.py:95-96 computes `default_out` and reads `DIAG_MATRIX_PATH`; the test asserts on source text only, so a refactor that preserves the unique-per-process/override behavior but changes the literal would fail the test — a change-detector (Rule 4).
ABSENCE: no assertion that two invocations yield distinct output paths, and no assertion that setting DIAG_MATRIX_PATH overrides the default — the actual added behavior is untested.
advisory.finding: test_diag_runaway_matrix_default_output_is_unique_per_process is a source-grep, not a behavior test: it asserts the .py source-under-test contains the literal string f".rebar/scratch/diag_matrix-{os.getpid()}.csv" rather than exercising the code. It would break on a behavior-preserving refactor (e.g. building the path via os.path.join or a helper) while the observable behavior — a unique per-process CSV path and a working DIAG_MATRIX_PATH override — is never verified. Unlike the push_err test, nothing here is executed.
scenarios: Refactoring the path construction (helper/os.path.join) with identical runtime behavior breaks this test.
A regression where DIAG_MATRIX_PATH is ignored, or getpid() is dropped so the path is fixed again, would NOT be caught as long as the literal string remains anywhere in the file.
advisory.suggested_fix: Import/exercise the path-selection logic (or run the script twice with different PIDs and with DIAG_MATRIX_PATH set) and assert the resulting Path values are unique-per-process and honor the override, rather than asserting on the source text.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Narrow the AGENTS.md test to assert only a stable structural anchor (e.g. the heading) if a machine consumer depends on it, or drop the prose-fragment assertions that merely lock wording.
evidence: tests/unit/test_per_session_scratch_guidance.py:21 `assert "Never redirect logs or evidence to a fixed `/tmp/<name>` path" in text`
tests/unit/test_per_session_scratch_guidance.py:22 `assert "overwrites or interleaves another session's evidence" in text`

Rule-5 structural exception applies only when a NON-HUMAN consumer branches on the exact token; these are prose sentences with no parser/registry/CI consumer, so the grep guards wording, not a contract.
advisory.finding: test_agents_guidance_prescribes_per_session_scratch_example asserts exact prose wording of AGENTS.md (a heading and multiple sentence fragments) that is consumed only by humans/LLMs, not a non-human parser. This is a change-detector on the author's wording: any rephrase that preserves the guidance breaks it, and it verifies no observable code behavior.
scenarios: A wording tweak to the AGENTS.md guidance (same meaning) fails the test.
The example shell snippet stays wrong but the prose sentences match — test still passes.
